clue.text: Old price of cereal in Corinth perhaps

parts.note: Corinth is a city of Greece, abbreviated GR
oats are a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A question about what grain once cost in an ancient Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cereal 'in Corinth' is Greek cereal, so the abbreviation for Greece goes in front of the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: The groat was an old English fourpenny coin, so a sum once charged for things.

clue.text: Rock as place of sacrifice under great rising river

indicators.note: in a down entry under puts this piece below the others
in a down entry rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: great means big
an altar is where offerings are sacrificed

explanation.surface: A rocky spot where sacrifices were made beneath a mighty river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' reads a word upwards and 'under' places a piece below; 'Rock' is the territory's familiar nickname, not a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rock is the usual nickname of the British territory at Spain's southern tip.

clue.text: Lightest of cats?

parts.note: the snow leopard has a name that is also one of the smallest imperial weights

explanation.surface: Which cat weighs least?
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called by this name, which is a small unit of weight.

clue.text: When things look dim, remedy with gilt

indicators.note: to remedy is to put right, so these letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to brighten a gloomy look with gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remedy' rearranges WITH GILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, the half-light after sunset, is when everything looks dim.

clue.text: Exquisite, conservative sort of verse

parts.note: an exquisite is an over-refined dandy, which the eighteenth century called a macaroni

explanation.surface: A description of refined, traditional poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exquisite' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a fop, as in the Yankee Doodle song's macaroni.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaronic verse mixes Latin with vernacular words for comic effect.

clue.text: Or as a — defensive to a house " (Richard II)

definitions.text: Or as a — defensive to a house " (Richard II)

parts.words: Or as a — defensive to a house " (Richard II)
parts.note: fill the gap in John of Gaunt's 'sceptred isle' speech, where the sea guards England like a castle's water barrier

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Richard II with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt compares the sea round England to a ditch of water guarding a castle.

clue.text: Love's humble home with a bird-some dish!

parts.note: the saying 'love in a cottage' makes a cottage the humble home of romance
pie is the old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: A lovers' modest house with a bird in it, served up as a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE is an old name for the magpie.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage pie is a British dish of minced beef topped with mashed potato.

clue.text: Fact one omitted-property in land

indicators.note: omitted means the following piece is taken out

parts.note: fact means reality
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A legal fact about land ownership with a detail left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted' takes I out of REALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is real estate, landed property as opposed to personal goods.

clue.text: Sugar cane -a bit best cut out for processing in Central America

indicators.note: the letters of best are cut out of the first words and what remains is processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sugar cane, the best of it trimmed, is refined in a Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: SUGAR CANE A BIT, less B, E, S, T ('cut out'), leaves UGARCANAI, which 'for processing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaragua is a republic of Central America.

clue.text: County girl's college

explanation.surface: A college for county girls.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a county in western Ireland, a woman's first name and a Cambridge college.

clue.text: Does Francois need a good liver to be one ?

definitions.text: Does Francois need a good liver to be one ?

parts.words: Does Francois need a good liver to be one ?
parts.note: a Frenchman's phrase for someone who lives well translates literally as 'good liver', so the organ joke is a translation joke

explanation.surface: A medical question about whether a Frenchman's health depends on his liver.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a person who enjoys food, drink and high living.

clue.text: Current make of car in West Africa

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: a make of something here means a remaking, so the letters of the car are reworked

explanation.surface: A motoring note on which brand of car is driven in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make of' reads as a car's brand but tells you to rearrange CAR into CRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana, on the West African coast.

clue.text: Rome and Berlin imprisoned the French saint

indicators.note: imprisoned means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the wartime alliance of Italy and Germany was called the Rome-Berlin Axis
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A wartime story of the Axis powers jailing a French holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' looks like it describes the saint, but it is the French article, which the wartime alliance 'imprisoned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Alexis of Rome is a fifth-century holy man venerated as 'the man of God'.

clue.text: Walter's about right about this section of garden

indicators.note: the first about means the surname goes around the next letter

parts.note: Walter Pater was the Victorian essayist and critic; read with 's as 'is'
re is Latin for 'about', concerning

explanation.surface: Someone named Walter being roughly correct about a part of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter is the Victorian critic Walter Pater; the first 'about' is a container, the second the Latin word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal ornamental flower-bed layout in a garden.

clue.text: Adam follows his role with Eve as farmer

indicators.note: follows puts this word after the other piece

parts.note: Adam was Eve's husband
Adam was the first man

explanation.surface: Adam's part as Eve's partner turned him into a tiller of the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' places the first man after his role with Eve; husbandry is the old word for farming.
explanation.definitionFit: A husbandman is an old word for one who tills the soil.

clue.text: A hunter's an unusual guest of Venus

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A hunter turns out to be an unexpected visitor to the goddess of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of A HUNTERS AN.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend and Wagner's opera, the minnesinger Tannhauser lives as a guest in Venus's mountain, the Venusberg.

clue.text: Poetic bird's reply?

parts.note: in Poe's poem the raven gives the same one-word answer to every question

explanation.surface: What does a bird in a poem say back?
explanation.definitionFit: The raven in Poe's poem answers every question with this word meaning 'never again'.

clue.text: Money-changing charge one's seen in a Japanese game

indicators.note: seen in means this letter sits inside the following words

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game of stones
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A banking fee spotted in a Japanese pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: I sits inside A plus GO.
explanation.definitionFit: An agio is the premium or fee paid when exchanging one currency for another.

clue.text: Omission of the periscope's function

definitions.meaning: a periscope lets one see over obstacles

explanation.surface: Missing something is what a periscope does.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless slip, and literally the seeing over things that a periscope provides.

clue.text: Girl with heavenly hair finds draught strangely pleasant

indicators.note: strangely means those letters come in an odd order

parts.note: draught beer is beer from the cask
pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A girl with lovely hair finds a pint oddly agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns BEER into BERE. The constellation Coma Berenices is Berenice's Hair, set in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Berenice's hair was placed among the stars as the constellation Coma Berenices.

clue.text: Wildly enthusiastic for a = vegetarian it appears

indicators.note: it appears says the answer shows up inside the words just before

explanation.surface: Someone getting very excited on behalf of a vegetarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in foR A VEgetarian.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave review is an extravagantly enthusiastic one.

clue.text: Old boy with two R's to rub out

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
of the 'three Rs', reading and writing are the two that make someone able to read and write

explanation.surface: A former pupil who can erase things.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are reading, writing and arithmetic; having the first two makes one LITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe away or destroy all trace of something.

clue.text: Little room near source of Thames

parts.note: near means close

indicators.note: the source of a river is its start, so the first letter

explanation.surface: A small room close to where the Thames rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'source of Thames' is its first letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small private room or cupboard.

clue.text: Charlie Girl, one of two in USA

definitions.meaning: the female form of the name Charles
the US has a North and a South state of this name

explanation.definitionFit: The name is the feminine Latin form of Charles, and North and South are two US states so named.

clue.text: Scale of one doctor-under a hundred quid

indicators.note: in a down entry under puts the earlier pieces below the next ones

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quid is a pound, abbreviated L from Latin libra
one is the Roman numeral I
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor's fee scale of less than a hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is British slang for a pound, abbreviated L; 'under' sets I and MB below C and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or peak is to ascend it.

clue.text: Wheel inventor' (fair clue)

parts.note: the fair hint points to the big fairground wheel, named after the American engineer who built the first one

explanation.surface: The inventor of the wheel, with a hint that the clue is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington Gale Ferris built the first great observation wheel for the 1893 Chicago fair.

clue.text: Being sorry for downfall? Grand !

parts.note: downfall means ruin
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Regretting a collapse that cost a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand is a common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, so rueing is feeling sorry.

clue.text: One point is made by, an Oxford magazine

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A remark that an Oxford periodical makes a single argument.
explanation.walkthrough: S is a compass point, south.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the Oxford University student magazine, named after the Thames at Oxford.

clue.text: Smith fires them-for playing around ?

definitions.meaning: a blacksmith heats metal bars and tools in the forge
golf clubs used for playing a round

explanation.surface: A blacksmith dismissing workers for fooling about.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith heats bars of metal in the forge, and golfers carry clubs of that name for a round.

clue.text: Doubt Bond's boss was born on Friday

parts.note: M is James Bond's chief in the Fleming novels
the nursery rhyme says Friday's child is loving and giving

explanation.surface: Uncertainty about whether 007's chief was born on a Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child' says Friday's child is loving and giving, so one born on Friday IS GIVING.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or apprehension.

clue.text: First milk might harm honey-hunting Pooh

definitions.meaning: the colostrum a cow gives just after calving
Winnie-the-Pooh raids hives for honey and risks being stung

explanation.surface: A warning that the bear's honey raids could hurt him.
explanation.definitionFit: Colostrum from a newly calved cow has this name, and insect stings would hurt a bear raiding a hive.

clue.text: Retiring soldier in the crew

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in means the soldier goes inside the word 'the'

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier leaving the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reverses the whole thing after 'in' has put the soldier inside; a rowing crew of eight is called an eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of eight oarsmen is itself called an eight.
